results.content:
Title: Building Cross-Platform CI/CD Actions with Docker - DEV Community
Cover image for Building Cross-Platform CI/CD Actions with Docker. # Building Cross-Platform CI/CD Actions with Docker. Last week I got hit by a headache - our perfectly tuned Lingo.dev GitHub Actions workflow couldn't run on a contributor's GitLab instance. So I went on a quest to build a cross-platform CI automation that runs on GitHub, GitLab, and Bitbucket (and possibly others too!). The solution started as a simple GitHub Action but evolved into something more powerful when we needed to support multiple code hosting platforms. Starting Simple: Run JavaScript in GitHub Actions. ### Running a GitHub Action. Let's start with the simplest possible GitHub Action - one that runs a JavaScript file. Create a new GitHub repository (e.g., `hello-world-action` like my example here) with these files:. Now, let's create a more sophisticated action that runs TypeScript code. # Run the action. `docker build -t hello-world-action .`. `docker run hello-world-action`. Now comes the most interesting part - running your action on other platforms. uses: docker/build-push-action@v5. ### Github Actions. To use this action in GitHub Actions of another repository, create a workflow file in `.github/workflows/hello.yml` (see GitHub Actions workflow syntax documentation):. If you need to run this action on GitHub Actions only, there is no need to build and push the Docker image. GitHub Actions will build the Docker container directly from the Dockerfile specified in your `action.yml` file on each workflow run. However, if you plan to use this action on other CI platforms like GitLab or Bitbucket, you'll need to publish the Docker image as shown above. Since we published our Docker image in a public Github Container Registry, we can run this on any platform that supports Docker images. We built an action to run automated Lingo.dev localization for your web and mobile apps on any CI platform. You can build reusable actions and easily integrate them into your workflows regardless of the code hosting platform you are using. It contains the action - you can run it on GitHub, GitLab and Bitbucket. We've seen how to evolve from a simple shell-based GitHub Action to a sophisticated TypeScript action that can run anywhere.

results.title: Local Run Github Action with Artifact: Lessons from a Cross-Platform Electron Build
results.content: Local Run Github Action with Artifact: Lessons from a Cross-Platform Electron Build. Act lets you run GitHub Actions locally, so you can validate your workflows before pushing anything. In my recent project — building and releasing a React + Electron app for macOS, Windows, and Linux — Act was a game-changer. In last my case, I need to build and release my react electron project for Windows and Linux. Act + Docker: Custom Image for Local CI. From the root _Dockerfile_ and run build to build with the name of image as you want. And we can run act with that new docker image to run locally test the github workflow. Last but not least we need to create directory to our host machine, that can be use by act as artifact target. I split the env setup to different action called setup, that action will catch all vars from our **_Github and secrets_** and create file _.env.production_. #.github/actions/setup/action.yml. description: "Injects REACT_APP_* and PUBLIC_URL into .env.production for CRA builds". - uses: actions/setup-node@v4. - uses: ./.github/actions/setup # <- load the env. - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4. C an you see**.build** will load the env via **_.github/actions/setup_**, and will build and upload to artifact via **_actions/upload-artifact@v4_**, first thing I zip the ./build to makes sure the structure on who use must be like **_./build/**/*_**because CRA expecting that structure the be exists. - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4. - run: unzip electron-build.zip. - uses: actions/setup-node@v4. - uses: ./.github/actions/setup # <- load env. # runs-on: windows-latest <- using it on github runner. runs-on: ubuntu-latest # <- using it on act. - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4. - run: unzip electron-build.zip. - uses: actions/setup-node@v4. - uses: ./.github/actions/setup # <- load env. T hen here **.release-*** will download the artifact using **_actions/download-artifact@v4_**and unzip the .zip. Load again the env via **_github/actions/setup_**, and release and publish the electron app. If you’re building cross-platform apps or just want cleaner CI/CD workflows, I highly recommend integrating Act into your development process.
